subject: Fixed effects multinomial regression gives duplicated values for intercept and slope coefficients

messages.author: df65534f41c91ca2
messages.subject: Fixed effects multinomial regression gives duplicated values for intercept and slope coefficients
parts:
I am trying to perform multinomial regression with a simple fixed effect (two groups). Let n be the number of samples (which belong to either group) and d be the number of features. My observed data is a (n x d) matrix of counts. My covariance matrix has dimensionality n x 2 (the first column representing the intersect as all ones, and the second representing the group to which a sample belongs as zeros or ones). The corresponding matrix of coefficients beta has dimensionality 2 x (d-1), as I am using the logit link to the matrix theta_prime, which can then be transformed to the parameter theta for the multinomial, the entries of which lie in the simplex.
My problem is that the estimated parameters beta are always a matrix of two repeated rows, and I don't know why. I show below an extreme case in which the true betas for the fixed effects are zero (i.e. the two groups give the same output).

File FE_multinomial.cpp:
// Simple fixed effects multinomial regression.
// partially inspired by https://figshare.com/articles/C_code_needed_for_running_R_code/4836503
#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{

  Type nll;           // Define variable that holds the return value (neg. log. lik)
  nll = Type(1.2);    // Assign value 1.2; a cast is needed.

  DATA_MATRIX(Y);
  DATA_INTEGER(d);
  DATA_INTEGER(n);
  DATA_MATRIX(x);
  PARAMETER_MATRIX(beta);
  int d_min1 = d - 1;
  int d_min2 = d - 2;

 
  matrix<Type> theta_prime(n,d_min1); // The probabilities of each event
  theta_prime = x * beta;

  vector<Type> Q(n); // The probabilities of each event
  for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
    Q(i) = 0;
    for(int j=0;j<d_min1;j++){
      Q(i) += exp(theta_prime(i,j));
    }
  }

  matrix<Type> theta(n,d); // The probabilities of each event
  for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
    for(int j=0;j<d_min1;j++){
      theta(i,j) = exp(theta_prime(i,j))/(Type(1.0)+Q(i));
    }
    theta(i,d_min1) = Type(1.0)/(Type(1.0)+Q(i));
  }

  REPORT(theta)

  for(int i=0; i<n; i++){ // Multinomial draws
    vector<Type> ith_row = Y.row(i);
    vector<Type> theta_i = theta.row(i);
    nll = -(dmultinom(ith_row, theta_i, true));
  }
  return nll;

}

My R file:

library(TMB)
#---------------------------------------------------------#
softmax = function(x){
  if(is.null(dim(x))){
    ## vector
    sum_x = sum(exp(x))
    exp(x)/sum_x
  }else{
    ## matrix
    sum_x = rowSums(exp(x))
    sweep(exp(x), 1, sum_x, '/')
  }
}

reflect_matrix = function(m){
  m[nrow(m):1,]
}
#---------------------------------------------------------#
compile("FE_multinomial.cpp", "-std=gnu++17")
dyn.load(dynlib("FE_multinomial"))
#---------------------------------------------------------#
# Create data
n = 100
d = 4
beta = rbind(rgamma(d-1, 1, 1),rgamma(d-1, 1, 2))
beta = rbind(rgamma(d-1, 1, 1), 0) ## setting slopes to 0, to give the most extreme example
## create a (n x 2) matrix. The first column are all zeros (intercept) and the second are 0 and 1 depending on the fixed effect value
x = cbind(1, sample(c(0,1), n, replace = TRUE))
true_theta = softmax(cbind(x %*% beta + matrix(rnorm(n*(d-1), mean = 0.5, sd=0.01), ncol=(d-1)), 0))
data <- list(Y = t(apply(true_theta, 1, function(p) rmultinom(1, 300, p))), n=n, d=d, x=x)
parameters <- list(
 beta = matrix(rbind(rep(1,d-1), rep(1,d-1)), nrow=2)
)
#---------------------------------------------------------#
# Run
obj <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL="FE_multinomial")
obj$hessian <- TRUE
opt <- do.call("optim", obj)
opt
opt$hessian
obj$he()
sdreport(obj)

## PROBLEM: the beta estimate shows a matrix with two identical rows, i.e. the slopes (fixed effect) which were simulated to be zero have a value equal to the intercept
betas_estimate = matrix(opt$par, nrow=2)
betas_estimate

Any help is much appreciated.
Lena
